key_insight: A single safety alignment step can be propagated across languages by enforcing multilingual consistency, enabling LLMs to behave safely in many languages without large per-language supervision.
problem_solved: Scaling safety alignment to many languages is costly and brittle: existing approaches require extensive target-language supervision or pairwise alignment with high-resource languages, limiting scalability and coverage.
method: Perform alignment once (e.g., in a high-resource language) and enforce multilingual consistency so aligned behavior is preserved under translation or cross-lingual prompts.

Leverage resource-efficient consistency objectives and lightweight cross-lingual data (e.g., translated or synthetic examples) to propagate safety signals instead of collecting large target-language annotations.
Validate transfer of safety via multilingual evaluation to ensure aligned behaviors hold across diverse languages and threat scenarios.
impact: Practitioners can achieve broader multilingual safety with far lower annotation and engineering cost, making safe LLM deployment across linguistic communities more practical and scalable.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: single-language alignment -> multilingual consistency module -> multilingual-safe model

paper_title: Align Once, Benefit Multilingually: Enforcing Multilingual Consistency for LLM Safety Alignment
paper_authors: Yuyan Bu, Xiaohao Liu, ZhaoXing Ren, Yaodong Yang, Juntao Dai
